answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to maintain a unique activity history tied to a non-transferable reputation score that rises like a tide only with verified original contributions. An attacker who tries to wander across many fake identities must produce distinct, high-quality work for each one—using a personal quill of creativity and compute—because peer graders reject near-duplicates. This multiplies the attacker's costs linearly with the number of sybils, while honest agents pay only once.
